rows: Tree down on the Highway 59 bridge over the Colorado River.
Golf ball size hail nearly covered the ground.
Strong wind gusts knocked down two power lines.
Damage to several smaller shed structures with significant damage to one large shed-barn structure. Minor damage to a local ball park's grandstand metal roofing.
Large tree down across a small residential porch structure.
Damage to large barn's metal roofing off of CR 434.
A parked 18-wheeler tractor trailer was blown over at the intersection of Highway 59 and FM 441 near Hilje. The driver suffered minor injuries.
Golfball size hail was observed in the town of Wharton.
A large barn (100 feet X 150 feet) was leveled due to strong thunderstorm wind gusts.
Penny to quarter size hail was observed in Wharton and lasted for approximately twenty minutes.
Thunderstorm winds downed tree limbs and power lines throughout the city of Wharton. Several streets and highways, including U.S. 59 southbound at the Colorado bridge, were blocked.
Golf ball size hail was observed on FM 1096 one mile from FM 1301.
A small barn was destroyed with a tenth of a mile long debris path.
Strong thunderstorm winds caused major roof damage to a residential home on the 400 block of Lewis Street in East Bernard.
Trees and power lines were blown down near the community of New Taiton.

Thunderstorm winds damaged or destroyed numerous barns in the New Taiton area about 1 mile around the intersection of Texas Highway 71 and FM 961. The winds also downed numerous trees and tree limbs along with 9 power poles. Around 150 acres of Maize and corn were also destroyed.
A tree was downed off of New Gulf Road.
A severe thunderstorm produced strong winds that blew down a billboard along Business 59 near Louise.
Several trees were reported downed along with damage to a telephone pole.
A tornado briefly touched down to the northwest of Wharton. There was no damage.
Downed trees blocked roadways at the intersection of Avenue A and Texas, Cornell and Elm, and in the 800 block of North Alabama in the city of Wharton.
Numerous branches, trees and power lines down scattered over large area, mainly north of 59. Fourteen thousand homes were left without power.
A pulse severe thunderstorm produce strong winds that downed power lines in East Bernard.
Severe thunderstorm winds downed large tree limbs onto power lines and cars in the East Bernard area.
Severe thunderstorms produced ping pong sized hail in the East Bernard area.
A trailer home and shed were destroyed near the intersection of County Road 216 and County Road 225.
Power lines were downed near Hungerford.
A severe thunderstorm produced quarter sized hail.
A severe thunderstorm produced quarter to golf ball sized hail.
A severe thunderstorm produced quarter to golf ball sized hail.
A severe thunderstorm produced golf ball sized hail near the intersection of FM 1301 and Pledger.
A severe thunderstorm downed trees on Highway 60.
Penny sized hail was observed on County Road 428 just south of Wharton.
Thunderstorm winds knocked down trees and blew windows out of homes in the town of Hungerford near County Road 218 and Highway 60.
Quarter sized hail damaged an agricultural field near the intersection of CR 407 and CR 414.
Trees were downed and there was damage to a barn on the east end of CR 272 near the San Bernard River.
Thunderstorm winds downed a tree in El Campo.
Dime sized hail was reported in the El Campo area.
Thunderstorm wind gust was near the intersection of FM 961 and Highway 71.
Penny sized hail was reported at the Wharton County Fairgrounds.
Nickel sized hail was reported in the Wharton area.
A severe thunderstorm wind tore off a part of a mobile home roof on FM 1301.
Thunderstorm wind damage was reported near County Road 216 and Machaville Road. There was some tree damage and home window damage.

This EF-0 tornado destroyed three sheds. Three residences also sustained structural damage. Irrigation equipment was damaged as the tornado crossed a grass field. Trees and power lines were downed, and parts of County Road 100 were blocked by debris.
Dime size hail was reported at the intersection of CR 131 and CR 152.
Quarter sized to golf ball size hail near the intersection of County Roads 123 and 154.
Power lines were downed near the intersection of West Norris Street and West Loop Street.

Brief touchdown. Tornado Damage Signature on radar.
Trees down along a southeast to northwest path. Horse trailer overturned. Tornado caught on video.

Tornado began as a weak EF0 in East Bernard then tracked NW across SH 90 where it strengthened to EF1 snapping the trunks of several large mature oak and pecan trees. A house suffered significant brick facade damage to one side of the home. Four apartments were damaged on college…
Thunderstorm wind gusts blew down some fencing around the town of Lane City.
There was southwest to northeast oriented wind damage to a barn and a shed.
Quarter sized hail was reported near New Taiton.
There were trees downed with two of them blocking roadways.
Near Spanish Camp, there was trailer damage, trees were uprooted, 2x4's were wedged into the ground and there was debris on power lines.
Houses were damaged in the East Bernard area close to Highway 60.
Straight-line wind gusts destroyed a barn and caused widespread tree damage near the intersection of FM 2614 and CR 265.
Trees were downed by strong thunderstorms wind gusts.
Wind gusts collapsed a metal bleacher at the East Bernard High School.

Multiple reports and videos from the public showed a tornado on the ground near El Campo.||Surveys found outbuildings damaged near County Road 405. One of which was well constructed and had major roof damage indicative of EF1 wind speeds.

An EF-0 tornado with winds of 75 mph began just east of Burr and produced some minor tree damage along its path as it travelled west across CR 117. An older shed also had its roof blown off along CR 111.
